items.stem: An accountant feels pressured by a manager to misstate results. The primary threat to ethical behaviour here is:

options.rationale: Correct: pressure from a superior is an intimidation threat.
Self-review involves reviewing one's own prior work.
Familiarity arises from close relationships over time.
Advocacy involves promoting a client's position.

items.explanation: Correct: pressure from a superior is an intimidation threat.

items.stem: Which two are fundamental principles of professional accounting ethics? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: integrity is a fundamental principle.
Correct: objectivity is a fundamental principle.
Personal gain is not an ethical principle.
Blind loyalty can conflict with integrity and objectivity.

items.explanation: Correct: integrity is a fundamental principle.

options.text: A reasonable observer must also perceive the accountant as unbiased
options.rationale: Correct: perceived independence protects public trust.

options.text: Only the accountant's private intentions count
options.rationale: Appearance to others matters, not just intentions.

options.text: Appearance is irrelevant if no law is broken
options.rationale: Appearance affects trust even where nothing illegal occurs.

items.explanation: Correct: perceived independence protects public trust.
